ADA TITLE II DEADLINE LOOKUP

Which ADA Title II website deadline applies to you?

State and local governments must make websites and mobile apps meet WCAG 2.1 AA under ADA Title II. The exact date depends on your entity's type and population. Enter yours below. Once you know your date, generate a WCAG 2.1 AA evidence record from an axe-core scan to start documenting progress toward it, or see how this compares to an installed widget like accessiBe.


  

  
Common questions
What is the ADA Title II website accessibility deadline for my city or county?
State and local government entities with a total population of 50,000 or more have until April 26, 2027 to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Entities with a population under 50,000, and any special district government of any size, have until April 26, 2028. These dates come from the Department of Justice's 2026 interim final rule extending the original 2024 compliance dates by one year.
Does a school district, water district, or fire district get the small-entity deadline automatically?
Yes. Any special district government — school, water, fire, transit, or other special-purpose district — has until April 26, 2028 regardless of the population it serves, under the same DOJ rule.
What standard do I actually need to meet?
WCAG 2.1 Level AA, which the DOJ's rule (28 CFR 35.200) adopts as the technical standard for web content and mobile apps covered by ADA Title II.
Is this legal advice?
No. This is a plain-language read of a published federal rule extension, not legal advice, and it does not review your specific facts. Confirm the current date, and whether it applies to your entity, with your own counsel or ADA coordinator, and check the Federal Register / ada.gov directly — an interim rule can change.

You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it. It does not determine whether a site is compliant.

ADA TITLE II WEBSITE ACCESSIBILITY EVIDENCE

Turn an axe scan into a Title II evidence record.

Paste an axe-core JSON export from your government website to get a dated summary split into WCAG 2.1 AA required findings and best-practice extras. Nothing leaves this browser. Not sure which deadline applies to your entity? Look up your ADA Title II compliance date. Considering an accessibility widget instead of, or alongside, documenting your own scans? See how this evidence report differs from accessiBe. Formatting a Shopify storefront scan instead? The Shopify accessibility evidence report turns the same kind of axe-core JSON into a dated storefront record. Preparing a procurement VPAT/ACR for a software product rather than a government website? See the VPAT / Accessibility Conformance Report generator instead -- it formats your own self-reported WCAG conformance answers into the standardized procurement document. The PDFs your site links are "web content" under this same rule too -- see the PDF accessibility tag checker for a no-upload evidence report on a document's own tag structure.

Paste axe JSON

Your report will appear here.

Common questions

Does this evidence record prove my government website is ADA Title II compliant?

No. It formats whatever axe-core found into a dated, readable record split into WCAG 2.1 AA required findings and best-practice extras — it does not run a scan itself, does not check anything axe-core cannot detect (screen-reader usability, keyboard traps, and most manual-review items are outside any automated tool's reach), and does not determine legal compliance. Automated testing typically finds a minority of WCAG issues. Treat this as documentation of one automated test at one point in time, not a compliance certificate.

What compliance date applies to my city, county, school, or special district?

It depends on your entity's population and type. Use the deadline lookup: large state/local government entities (population 50,000+) have until April 26, 2027; smaller entities and any special district government (school, water, fire, transit, or other special-purpose district) have until April 26, 2028, per the U.S. Department of Justice's 2026 rule extension.

Where do I get the axe JSON to paste in?

Run axe-core (the axe DevTools browser extension, axe-core CLI, or a similar automated tool) against your site and export its JSON results — this page only formats output you already generated elsewhere, it does not crawl or scan your site itself.

Does my scan data get uploaded anywhere?

No. The JSON you paste is parsed and formatted entirely in your browser; nothing is sent to a server. Usage counting only tallies anonymous feature events in localStorage, with an opt-out checkbox above.

vs-accessibe.html.text:
← ADA Title II Website Accessibility Evidence Report

This evidence report vs. accessiBe

Two different shapes: accessiBe installs an ongoing widget and audit subscription on your live government website. This page formats an axe-core scan you already ran into a dated, portable WCAG 2.1 AA evidence record for ADA Title II, free and local — no widget, no installation, nothing shipped to residents.

What each product is for

accessiBe sells accessWidget, a JavaScript widget installed on a live site that applies automated interface adjustments and AI-driven remediation aimed at WCAG conformance every time a visitor loads the page, alongside audits, a generated accessibility statement, and ongoing monitoring — described on accessiBe's own site as a paid, ongoing subscription product marketed to government and education customers preparing for ADA Title II and Section 508. It is built for an entity that wants an installed layer running on the site itself, plus a vendor relationship for audits and monitoring over time. accessiBe's own current pricing and contract terms are not repeated here, since this session cannot verify today's figures against accessiBe's site; only its well-documented product shape — an installed widget plus an audit/monitoring subscription — is described.

This tool does none of what accessWidget does. It installs nothing on a site, changes nothing a resident sees, and has no ongoing subscription. It takes the axe-core JSON export you already generated somewhere else — the axe DevTools browser extension, the axe-core CLI, or a similar tool — and formats it into a dated, readable evidence record split into WCAG 2.1 AA required findings and best-practice extras, plus a link to look up which Title II deadline (April 2027 or April 2028) applies to your entity. It runs entirely in your browser, needs no account and no site access, and uploads nothing you paste.

QuestionWhere to answer it
I want an installed layer that adjusts my live government website's interface for residents, on every page load, without a developer fixing the templates.accessiBe — that is the installed-widget job accessWidget is built for.
I already ran an axe-core scan and want a dated, readable Title II evidence record of what it found, to file or hand to a developer.This tool — paste the JSON, get the record, free and instant, nothing installed.
I want an ongoing vendor relationship: recurring audits, a generated accessibility statement, and monitoring over time.accessiBe or a comparable subscription service — this page has no memory between visits and no ongoing service.
I want to know exactly what my own axe-core scan found, split into what Title II's WCAG 2.1 AA standard actually requires versus best-practice extras.This tool — it reports only what the scan you supply contains, split the way the deadline lookup and evidence record describe.
I don't yet know whether my entity's Title II deadline is April 2027 or April 2028.The deadline lookup on this same free tool.
Do I need to install anything on my site, or give the tool access to it, to use it?This tool: no. accessWidget is installed directly on the site by design.

An entity can reasonably want both: an installed widget and audit subscription like accessiBe's for the live site experience, and a free local tool like this one for turning a specific axe-core run into a dated record that outlives any single dashboard. This page does not evaluate accessWidget's effectiveness and makes no claim about whether an installed overlay satisfies ADA Title II or any other legal obligation — it only describes accessiBe's documented product shape and states what this tool does differently. Automated testing, with or without an overlay installed, typically finds a minority of WCAG issues; neither this tool nor an installed widget determines legal compliance on its own.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the formatting runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Does accessiBe make my government website ADA Title II compliant?

Installing accessiBe's accessWidget does not by itself prove compliance with ADA Title II's WCAG 2.1 AA standard, and this page makes no claim about accessWidget's effectiveness either way. accessWidget is a JavaScript widget, described on accessiBe's own site as an ongoing paid subscription, that applies automated interface adjustments and AI-driven remediation on a live site. Title II asks whether your web content and mobile apps actually conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, which is a question about the underlying page, not about which vendor's script is installed on top of it. This tool does not install anything or touch your live site at all — it takes an axe-core JSON export you already generated and turns it into a dated, readable evidence record split into what WCAG 2.1 AA requires and what goes beyond it, for your own compliance file.

Should I use this tool or accessiBe?

They are different shapes of product, and a government entity preparing for the April 2027/2028 Title II dates may reasonably use both. accessiBe sells accessWidget, an ongoing paid subscription installed on a live site, plus audits, a generated accessibility statement, and monitoring, marketed to government and education customers. This page has no widget, installs nothing, and changes nothing a resident sees. It takes an axe-core JSON export — from the axe DevTools browser extension, the axe-core CLI, or a similar automated tool — and formats it into a dated WCAG 2.1 AA evidence record you can file or hand to a developer, in your browser, free, with no account and nothing uploaded. An entity wanting an installed layer and an ongoing vendor relationship is buying a different product than one wanting a free, private, dated record of what one automated scan actually found.

Is this page affiliated with accessiBe?

No. This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by accessiBe, Inc. accessiBe and accessWidget are trademarks of accessiBe, Inc., named here only to describe what this tool is and is not, based on accessiBe's own public site.
